cards.label: ACT
cards.claim: A hybrid MOND cosmology with an 11 eV sterile neutrino can form realistic early structure
cards.people: Tomas Ondro, Nikolaos Samaras · affiliation not in source
cards.stage_headline: Stage 3 of 5: tested against a control.
cards.stage_note: Preprint, not peer reviewed. One group, no replication. Headline results not yet seen.
cards.impact_heading: IF TRUE, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: Early structure without cold dark matter, and a concrete lab target: a sterile neutrino near 11 eV.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: Hydrodynamical runs compare the model with ΛCDM (H0 = 67.8, Ωm ≈ 0.31) and its νHDM progenitor. The authors say it fits the third Planck CMB peak.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: The headline results, because our abstract was cut off. Whether another code reproduces them.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: An independent group with a different MOND code gets the same structure, or evidence turns up for a sterile neutrino near 11 eV.

details.heading: Would prove it wrong
details.text: Limits exclude an 11 eV sterile neutrino at the needed abundance, or structure forms at the wrong times or amounts.

follow.name: [Independent MOND simulation group]
follow.role: to identify, for a reproduction with a different code

cards.todo: Email both authors for the full results, the simulation code and the observable where their model and ΛCDM diverge most.
cards.rule_text: if they name one clean discriminating observable, invite them to speak.
cards.compare_text: Last week’s open thread: a comment argues a published 3.3σ kinematic SZ exclusion of deep MOND does not follow from its own calculation.

primary_link.label: arXiv: The formation of the first cosmic structures in hybrid Milgromian cosmology

cards.label: ACT
cards.claim: The strength of the surrounding electromagnetic field changes psi task performance
cards.people: Dean Radin (Institute of Noetic Sciences), Michelle Fauver, Glenn Hartelius · Journal of Parapsychology
cards.stage_headline: Stage 3 of 5: tested against a control.
cards.stage_note: Single-lab RCT, peer reviewed. No replication. We saw the title only, so the result is unknown.
cards.impact_heading: IF TRUE, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: A physical knob that turns a psi effect up or down would make it testable on demand.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: It is a randomized controlled trial in a reviewed journal, testing a moderator that can be manipulated.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: The direction and size of any effect, or whether field condition was blinded.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: A preregistered replication in another lab, blind to field condition, finds the same effect.

details.heading: Would prove it wrong
details.text: That replication finds no difference, or the effect disappears once field condition is blinded.

follow.name: Dean Radin
follow.role: Institute of Noetic Sciences, long record in experimental psi

follow.name: Glenn Hartelius
follow.role: co-author; also on a large NLP analysis of psilocybin reports this week

follow.name: Zoltan Kekecs
follow.role: ELTE, designed the Transparent Psi Project; a candidate to design a replication

cards.todo: Get the full paper. Check preregistration, whether the data are shared and how field condition was blinded.
cards.rule_text: if it reports a specific positive effect with a clear protocol, scope funding for an independent preregistered replication.
cards.compare_text: A 2025 three-study Bem replication (PLOS ONE) confirmed an anomaly once, then failed to repeat it in 217,800 trials. One confirmatory hit is not enough.

primary_link.label: Journal of Parapsychology: Effect of Electromagnetic Field Strength on Psi Performance

cards.label: WATCH
cards.claim: Golden-ratio and pentagonal rules predict the lepton mixing angles and recur in quark masses
cards.people: Jacek Ciborowski · affiliation not in source
cards.stage_headline: Stage 2 of 5: uses data, but no comparison group.
cards.stage_note: Single-author preprint. Fitted after the fact, with no underlying dynamics.
cards.impact_heading: IF TRUE, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: A hint of an underlying symmetry that sets fermion mixing and masses.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: Three explicit rules: T5(θ12) = 0, T5(θ23) = −1 and θ13 ≈ θ12·θ23/π. The author labels it semi-empirical.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: Whether the match is more than coincidence. The screener calls it numerological.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: New precision measurements converge on the predicted angles, or it makes a correct prediction it wasn’t tuned for.

details.heading: Would prove it wrong
details.text: Better measurements of θ12, θ23 or θ13 exclude the predicted values.

cards.todo: No outreach now. Check the predicted angles each time new neutrino oscillation results come out.
cards.rule_text: a prediction made in advance holds up.

primary_link.label: arXiv: Fine structure of fermion mixing and quark-mass hierarchies

cards.label: WATCH
cards.claim: High power density is a universal signature that can guide biosignature and technosignature searches
cards.people: Clément Vidal, Luciano Kadian · affiliation not in source
cards.stage_headline: Stage 2 of 5: uses data, but no comparison group.
cards.stage_note: Calculation with control populations. No anomaly found yet.
cards.impact_heading: IF TRUE, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: One metric for ranking where technosignature searches look first.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: Cataclysmic variables, neutron stars and transient black holes rank high, against young stars and supermassive black holes as controls.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: How the metric separates life or technology from ordinary accretion.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: A ranked search finds accretion behavior standard models can’t explain, and it persists.

details.heading: Would prove it wrong
details.text: Standard accretion physics explains every high-ranking system.

cards.todo: No outreach yet. Useful framing, but there is no testable anomaly.
cards.rule_text: a power-density-ranked search reports an unexplained, persistent anomaly.
cards.compare_text: Breakthrough Listen’s radio search of 3I/ATLAS could detect transmitters down to about 0.1 W and found no credible signal. Null results with stated sensitivity are the bar.

primary_link.label: arXiv: Power Density as a Universal Biosignature: An Application to the Stellivore Hypothesis

cards.label: WATCH
cards.claim: Late-time cosmic acceleration can arise from matter alone through Barrow-corrected horizon entropy
cards.people: Navaneeth Preman P K, Sarath Nelleri · affiliation not in source
cards.stage_headline: Stage 1 of 5: an idea, not yet tested.
cards.stage_note: Theory derived two ways. No fit to observational data.
cards.impact_heading: IF TRUE, HOW BIG A DEAL?

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: Modified Friedmann equations from Barrow entropy and Kaniadakis statistics. The authors also check the generalized second law and perturbation growth.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: Whether it fits any data, and how many free parameters it needs.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: A joint fit to supernova, BAO and growth data matches ΛCDM without extra parameters.

details.heading: Would prove it wrong
details.text: It can’t fit expansion and growth at once, or needs parameters excluded elsewhere.

follow.name: Navaneeth Preman P K, Sarath Nelleri

cards.todo: Nothing until the authors publish a fit to data.
cards.rule_text: a joint supernova, BAO and growth fit appears.

primary_link.label: arXiv: Matter-Only Late-Time Acceleration via Barrow Entropy in Kaniadakis Statistics

cards.label: CONTEXT
cards.claim: What survives of cold fusion is an active exotic-atom physics program, not an energy source
cards.stage_note: In the lab, materials-enhanced fusion at low energy is now measured, but no group shows net energy gain.
cards.impact_heading: IF TRUE, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: Compact neutron and heat sources from materials-driven fusion. Grid energy stays out of reach.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: Quanta reports a thriving exotic-atom research program, including muon-catalyzed fusion, in the area once tied to cold fusion.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: Which groups and results the piece names. Our excerpt didn’t say.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: Exotic-atom fusion keeps producing peer-reviewed results.

details.heading: Would change the conclusion
details.text: Independently replicated net excess energy from a low-energy nuclear process.

follow.name: Jeremy Munday
follow.role: UC Davis, corresponding author of the July 2026 sub-keV fusion paper

follow.name: Thomas Schenkel, Arun Persaud
follow.role: Berkeley Lab, co-authors of that paper

follow.name: Konrad Czerski
follow.role: University of Szczecin, earlier electron-screening measurements

cards.todo: Read the full Quanta piece and list the exotic-atom researchers it names. Add any with recent peer-reviewed results to contacts.
cards.rule_text: papers from ARPA-E’s LENR teams and awards under DARPA’s MARRS program on fusion rates in solids.
cards.compare_text: Karahadian et al., Nature Communications, Jul 18 2026: deuterium fusion in Pd and Ti foils plateaus below about 2.5 keV, over 10¹⁸ above bare-nucleus rates. The team says the rates are far too small for energy.

primary_link.label: Quanta Magazine: Is There Anything Left in the Dream of Cold Fusion?
